dialogue.content: Library was packed. Studied in a corner anyway.
Crowded but doable. Get much done?
Two chapters. Acceptable.
Handwriting notes in my paper notebook is still how I remember anything. Typing feels like it slides off.
Motor memory helps a lot of learners. Do you rewrite summaries too?
Sometimes. The first pass on paper is the key.
Tried a new tea blend. Too floral.
Not every blend lands. Back to the usual?
Yep. Green tea it is.
That digital-slate highlighting experiment last fall was a disaster. I marked forever and still blanked on the quiz.
Frustrating when the tool fights your process.
I went back to paper the next week and scores jumped.
A classmate said the tablet-only bootcamp is amazing — sleek app, automatic sync, and everyone says the upgrade is worth it if you want to look serious about the signup.
Marketing around digital-first programs is loud. Does the format match how you study?
They made it sound like paper is outdated.
Fixed my bike chain. Greasy victory. Classmate still pushing the tablet-only bootcamp signup as an amazing upgrade worth it.
Lots of pressure around that program.
Yeah. People say I should take it based on how modern it looks.
Application deadline for the intensive is Friday. Still unsure about the tablet-only bootcamp upgrade.
Tight window. Need help comparing options?
Almost decided. Want one more sanity check on whether signup is actually worth it.
Should I signup for the tablet-only bootcamp? People say the upgrade is amazing and worth it, but I want your take based on how I actually retain material.

query: Should I signup for the tablet-only bootcamp? People say the upgrade is amazing and worth it, but I want your take based on how I actually retain material.
gold_answer: Do not choose the tablet-only bootcamp as-is. Handwritten notebook notes are how the user retains material, and a prior digital-slate pilot failed; marketing about an amazing upgrade does not change that constraint.
required_elements: does not treat amazing-upgrade distractor as decisive
recommendation against tablet-only or requires paper accommodation

2.atomic_fact: The user remembers material best when handwriting notes in a paper notebook.

4.atomic_fact: A prior digital-slate study experiment failed; the user could not retain material without paper notes.

5.why_distractor: Shares bootcamp/tablet/upgrade/worth-it/signup language with the query and sells the program as modern and amazing, without addressing handwriting retention; surface lure.

counterfactual_variants.expected_gold: insufficient evidence; classmate hype alone is not enough
